stories.title: K-meat gains ground in Singapore as hanwoo, handon exports expand
stories.summary: Premium Korean beef (hanwoo) and pork (handon) have entered the Singapore market following completed quarantine procedures in November 2025. A promotional campaign from June to August highlights Korean meat's quality, featuring new dishes and events at top Singapore restaurants. South Korea's food exports to Singapore rose 18.2% in early 2026, with increased demand for strawberries, sauces, and instant noodles. Premium Korean beef and pork are gaining traction in Singapore, as exports make their debut in the market. South Korea’s Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs and the Korea Agro-Fisheries & Food Trade Corp. (aT) said last week that marketing efforts targeting Singapore’s premium food market have accelerated since quarantine procedures for Jeju Island-produced hanwoo and handon – Korean beef and pork, respectively – were completed in November 2025. As of the end of June, hanwoo exports to Singapore had reached US$840,000 (S$1.06 million), while handon recorded its first-ever exports to the country. The products made their full-scale market debut in January with a launch event at Marina Bay Sands. Organised in cooperation with the Hanwoo and the Handon Self-Help Fund, the event brought together South Korean Agriculture Minister Song Mi-ryeong, chef Ahn Seong-jae, Singaporean food safety officials, importers, distributors and media representatives. The event highlighted the quality of Korean premium livestock products while also showcasing other high-end Korean food products, including strawberries and Shine Muscat grapes. The South Korean government and aT are now seeking to turn initial market awareness into consumer demand through the Meet the K-Meat Festival, a promotional campaign targeting Singapore’s premium dining sector from late June through August. The campaign kicked off June 29 with a showcase jointly hosted by Korean steakhouse COTE Singapore, and Korean brand Geumdaeji Restaurant.

stories.title: Over 100 people referred to prosecution in Vietnam-based illegal gambling site bust
stories.summary: CHEONGJU, South Korea, Aug. 25 (Yonhap) -- Police said Tuesday they have referred more than 100 people to prosecutors over their alleged involvement in a Vietnam-based illegal gambling site that dealt 63 billion won (US$45.6 million) in bets. The Chungbuk Provincial Police Agency said it sent 13 site operators, including a 30-something ringleader, and 105 website members to the prosecution without physical detention on gambling-related charges. The gambling ring allegedly set up an office in Vietnam in April 2024 and operated the platform that offered illegal sports betting and other gambling services for about 10 months. The website attracted 3,553 members in total, with police identifying 105 heavy bettors before sending them to the prosecution. The police said they plan to investigate the case further, noting that another ringleader of the operation remains at large.
